title: Level 2: Credit Analysis and Appraisal
subtitle: Judge a borrower, size and structure a facility, grade the risk and defend a recommendation
summary: Take a mid-sized commercial request from spread statements to a committee-ready recommendation, using one Ethiopian manufacturer as a running case.
audience: Credit officers with 1 to 3 years of experience, junior credit analysts and branch managers in Ethiopian banks and microfinance institutions who have completed Level 1 or have equivalent experience.
objectives: Spread three years of statements and interpret trends in leverage, liquidity, profitability, activity and coverage
Estimate working capital need, size an overdraft and test term loan repayment with DSCR
Score a borrower on a five-parameter risk grading model
Structure collateral, equity, covenants and price to the risk
Write a credit analysis report and defend it before a credit committee

runningCase.name: Bole Edible Oil PLC
runningCase.text: Bole Edible Oil PLC refines and packs edible oil from imported crude oil. It has banked with Bank A for 6 years, holds a Birr 10.5 million overdraft and a term loan with regular repayment, and now asks to raise the overdraft to Birr 16 million and for a new Birr 9 million, 5-year term loan for an automatic packaging line. Its audited sales grew from Birr 60 million to Birr 84 million over three years, while operating margin fell from 9% to 6.5% and the overdraft grew from Birr 4.0 million to Birr 10.5 million. Each module takes the case one step further, from spreading to the committee decision.

modules.title: Financial statement analysis
modules.summary: Read three years of statements as a story of where cash came from and where it went, and spot when growth is eating a borrower's liquidity.
objectives: Spread three years of statements into a standard format, with tangible net worth, shareholder loans and one-off items adjusted
Compute and interpret liquidity, leverage, profitability, activity and coverage ratios
Explain where a borrower's cash went using receivable, inventory and payable days
Judge the quality of statements and classify an auditor's qualification as major or minor

lessons.title: Sales grew 40%: is that good news?
body: A credit officer is often shown a sales chart that only goes up. Growth feels safe, but growth has to be financed. Every extra Birr of sales usually needs more stock on the shelf and more money waiting with customers, and that money must come from somewhere: profit, the owners, suppliers or the bank.

Financial statement analysis is the habit of reading the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow together as one story. The question is never only "how much did they sell?" but "what did it cost to sell it, and who paid for the gap?"
points: Income statement: did each Birr of sales earn more or less than last year?
Balance sheet: who finances the business, owners or creditors, and is that changing?
Cash: did the business generate cash, or consume it while reporting a profit?

example.title: Tana Paper Products PLC
example.text: Tana Paper Products PLC in Bahir Dar grew sales 40% in one year, from Birr 25 million to Birr 35 million. Its owner, Mulugeta Assefa, proudly asked for a bigger overdraft. The analyst noticed that receivables had doubled because Tana had offered schools 90 days' credit to win tenders, and the overdraft had grown from Birr 3 million to Birr 7 million. The growth was real, but it was being paid for by the bank, not by profit.

lessons.tip: When sales jump, look first at receivables, inventory and the overdraft. If they grew faster than sales, the growth is borrowed.

lessons.title: Spreading: putting statements in one format
body: Spreading means re-casting every set of statements into the bank's standard format so that years and companies can be compared line by line. Borrowers' accountants use different headings, so the analyst rebuilds the figures before computing a single ratio.

Four adjustments matter most. Separate operating from non-operating items. Deduct intangible assets such as goodwill to arrive at tangible net worth. Treat shareholder loans as quasi-equity only if they are subordinated to the bank in writing; otherwise they are debt. Note one-off items, such as a gain on selling a truck, so they do not flatter the trend.

items.label: Collect
items.text: Latest three years, audited or provisional

items.label: Re-cast
items.text: Map every line into the bank's template

items.label: Adjust
items.text: Intangibles, shareholder loans, one-off items

items.label: Reconcile
items.text: Equity movement must match profit, capital and dividends

items.label: Analyze
items.text: Ratios, trends and peer comparison

regulation.source: A commercial bank's credit procedure manual (2025)
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual asks for the latest three years' audited or provisional financial statements with the business plan, and comparative statements for at least two consecutive years so that trend analysis is possible. The analyst must ask the customer to explain any big jump or drop.

worked.title: Reconciling Bole Edible Oil's equity (Birr thousands)
worked.note: Equity reconciles exactly, so no profit is missing and no unexplained reserve has appeared. If it did not reconcile, the analyst would ask why before going further.

scenario.title: A shareholder loan in the balance sheet
scenario.situation: Genet Bekele's company, Sheger Plastics PLC, shows a Birr 3 million loan from its shareholders in long-term liabilities. Genet says it is "really equity" and asks you to count it as net worth. There is no written subordination agreement.
scenario.question: How should you treat the Birr 3 million in your spread?
options: As debt, until the shareholders subordinate it to the bank in writing
As equity, because the shareholders say so
Delete it from the balance sheet
As a current liability due within the year
scenario.explain: A shareholder loan counts as quasi-equity only if it is subordinated to the bank in writing. Without that, the owners could repay themselves ahead of the bank, so it is debt. Deleting it or reclassifying it as current would misstate the balance sheet.

lessons.title: The five ratio families
body: Ratios turn a page of numbers into a few signals. They fall into five families, each answering one question about the borrower. No single ratio decides a loan; the families together tell the story.

A ratio means little alone. Compare it with the company's own trend, with sector norms and with the bank's grading thresholds. A current ratio of 1.5 may be comfortable for a retailer and weak for a manufacturer with slow stock.

items.label: Liquidity
items.text: Current ratio; quick ratio = (current assets minus inventory) / current liabilities

items.label: Leverage
items.text: Debt / tangible net worth; debt / total assets

items.label: Profitability
items.text: Gross, operating and net margin; ROA; ROE

items.label: Activity
items.text: Receivable, inventory and payable days; cash conversion cycle

items.label: Coverage
items.text: Interest coverage = EBIT / interest; DSCR

worked.title: Bole Edible Oil: key ratios FY1, FY2, FY3
worked.note: Sales grow strongly, but every margin and coverage ratio falls, and leverage rises in FY3.

lessons.tip: Always write the trend next to each ratio: stable, rising, falling. The committee reads the arrow before the number.

lessons.title: Reading Bole's story
body: Bole Edible Oil PLC refines and packs edible oil from imported crude oil. Its sales rose from Birr 60 million to Birr 84 million in two years, yet operating margin fell from 9% to 6.5%. Crude oil costs are rising faster than the prices Bole can charge, so each Birr of sales earns less.

Interest expense rose from Birr 1.2 million to Birr 2.1 million while operating profit stayed near Birr 5.5 million. Interest coverage therefore fell from 4.5 to 2.6 times. The current ratio looks stable at about 1.55 only because the overdraft grew alongside receivables and inventory: both sides of the ratio were inflated by bank borrowing.

visual.caption: Bole's interest coverage fell by more than 40% in two years while sales grew.

example.title: Why margins fell at Bole
example.text: Bole's general manager, Dawit Haile, explained at the site visit that crude palm oil prices in foreign currency rose, and the Birr cost of imports rose with them, while supermarkets in Addis Ababa resisted price increases. Gross margin slipped from 22% to 18%. The analyst noted this as the key risk: if the squeeze continues, coverage will fall below 2 and the grade will drop.

scenario.title: A stable current ratio
scenario.situation: A colleague reviewing Bole's file says: "The current ratio has been 1.55 for three years, so liquidity is fine." Over the same period the overdraft rose from Birr 4.0 million to Birr 10.5 million and receivables doubled.
scenario.question: What is the best response?
options: Agree: a stable current ratio proves stable liquidity
Ignore liquidity and focus only on collateral
Disagree: check activity ratios and cash flow, because bank borrowing grew both sides of the ratio
scenario.explain: Current assets and current liabilities can grow together with bank borrowing while stock and receivables become slower. Activity ratios and cash flow reveal the problem that the current ratio hides.

lessons.title: Where did the cash go? The cash conversion cycle
body: Activity ratios show how long cash is tied up in the trading cycle. Receivable days = receivables / sales x 365. Inventory days = inventory / cost of sales x 365. Payable days = payables / cost of sales x 365.

The cash conversion cycle is the number of days between paying for inputs and collecting cash from customers. When it lengthens, the business needs more working capital for the same sales, and someone has to fund it.

visual.caption: A longer cycle means more days of the business that must be financed.

worked.title: Bole Edible Oil: activity in days, FY1, FY2, FY3
worked.note: Bole now waits about 35 days longer to turn purchases into cash. Customers pay slower, stock piles up and suppliers are paid faster. The overdraft filled the gap, so part of the new request finances slower collections, not only growth.

example.title: A Merkato textile trader's long cycle
example.text: Hirut Alemu's textile trading business in Merkato held 120 days of stock because she bought whole containers to get a discount. Her receivable days were only 15. When the analyst computed her cycle at 105 days, Hirut realised the container discount was smaller than the overdraft interest on the extra stock. She moved to smaller, more frequent orders.

lessons.title: Quality of statements and the auditor's opinion
body: Not all statements carry the same weight. Audited statements by a licensed auditor rank above provisional statements, which rank above a commercial credit report. Read the auditor's opinion first: it tells you how far you can trust everything after it.

In the grading model used in this course, a disclaimer of opinion, negative tangible net worth, or a qualification larger than 15% of total assets is a major discrepancy (minus 5 points). A smaller qualification is minor (minus 2). Cross-check declared sales with VAT returns and bank account credits, and confirm with the audit firm in writing that the statements are genuine.

left.title: Audited statements
items: Confirm genuineness with the audit firm

right.title: Provisional statements
items: Sample-check against invoices, stock and bank credits

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/90/2024, Asset classification and provisioning (as cited in a commercial bank's credit manual)
regulation.text: Before granting loans of Birr 10 million or more to a borrower in business for at least one year, the bank must review the borrower's externally audited financial statements. A typical Ethiopian bank manual goes further and asks for audited statements from a total exposure of Birr 5 million, so the safe practice is to request them from Birr 5 million.

worked.title: Classifying Bole's FY3 audit qualification

rows.label: Doubtful receivables over one year old
Tangible net worth after writing them down

worked.note: The qualification is minor for grading, but it confirms the collection problem the activity ratios showed.

scenario.title: A disclaimer of opinion
scenario.situation: Kebede Woldemariam presents the audited statements of Kombolcha Steel Works PLC for a Birr 18 million overdraft renewal. The auditor has issued a disclaimer of opinion because stock records could not be verified.
scenario.question: How should the analyst treat these statements?
options: As audited and up to date, full score
As a minor discrepancy, minus 2 points
As a major discrepancy, minus 5 points, and seek further evidence before relying on them
Ignore the opinion because the figures look reasonable
scenario.explain: A disclaimer means the auditor could not form an opinion, so it is a major discrepancy (minus 5) and the figures cannot be relied on without further evidence such as a stock count and bank account credits.

takeaways: Growth must be financed: check whether receivables, inventory and the overdraft grew faster than sales.
Spread first, then compute: deduct intangibles, treat unsubordinated shareholder loans as debt and flag one-off items.
Read ratios as families and trends, compared with the company's own history, the sector and the bank's grading thresholds.
A stable current ratio can hide a liquidity problem when bank borrowing inflates both sides; the cash conversion cycle reveals it.
Read the auditor's opinion first: a disclaimer, negative tangible net worth or a qualification above 15% of total assets is a major discrepancy.

quiz.q: Why is the quick ratio more conservative than the current ratio?
options: It excludes inventory, the least liquid current asset
quiz.explain: The quick ratio removes inventory, which takes the longest to turn into cash.

quiz.q: Inventory is Birr 9 million and cost of sales is Birr 54 million. What are inventory days?
quiz.explain: 9 / 54 x 365 = about 61 days.

quiz.q: Operating margin fell from 9% to 6.5% while sales rose. Which is a likely cause?
options: A rise in the current ratio
Input costs rising faster than selling prices
quiz.explain: Rising input costs, price discounting, higher overheads or a change in product mix all squeeze operating margin.

quiz.q: What is tangible net worth?
options: Net worth minus intangible assets such as goodwill
quiz.explain: Tangible net worth deducts intangibles that a bank could not sell to recover a loan.

quiz.q: An auditor issues a disclaimer of opinion. How is it treated in grading?
quiz.explain: A disclaimer is a major discrepancy, minus 5, and the statements need further evidence.

quiz.q: Receivables are Birr 12.6 million and sales Birr 84 million. Receivable days are closest to:
quiz.explain: 12.6 / 84 x 365 = 54.75, about 54.8 days, Bole's FY3 figure.

modules.title: Cash flow, working capital and repayment capacity
modules.summary: Size a facility from the borrower's cash cycle and cash flow, not from what the customer asks for or what the collateral can carry.
objectives: Compute cash flow from operations and explain why a profitable firm can run short of cash
Estimate the working capital gap and size an overdraft with an owner's margin
Calculate and interpret the debt service coverage ratio for each year of a term loan
Design a repayment schedule, grace period and tenor that match the borrower's cash flow

lessons.title: Cash flow from operations
body: Profit is an opinion; cash is a fact. Cash flow from operations starts from net profit, adds back depreciation and other non-cash charges, then deducts the money absorbed by working capital.
A profitable company can still be short of cash if working capital absorbs it. When receivables and stock grow faster than payables, the business reports a profit while its bank balance falls.

visual.caption: Non-cash charges are added back; money tied up in the trading cycle is deducted.

worked.title: Bole Edible Oil: cash flow from operations (Birr thousands)

rows.label: FY2 on the same basis (2,982 + 1,600 minus 3,000 minus 3,000 + 500)

worked.note: Bole made a profit in both years but consumed cash, and the overdraft funded it.

example.title: A profitable flour mill with an empty account
example.text: Adama Flour Mill PLC reported a Birr 4 million profit, yet its owner, Tsegaye Mekonnen, could not pay his wheat supplier. Sales to government distributors were on 60-day credit and he had bought six months of wheat before a price rise. Profit plus depreciation was Birr 5.2 million, but Birr 6.5 million went into receivables and stock. Cash flow from operations was minus Birr 1.3 million.

lessons.title: The working capital gap and the owner's margin
body: To size an overdraft, project next year's receivables, inventory and payables from projected sales and target cycle days. The working capital gap is receivables plus inventory minus payables.

The borrower should finance part of the gap from long-term funds: this is the margin. A common teaching rule, to be replaced by your bank's own method, is that the bank funds up to 75% of the gap. The owners keep a stake in their own trading cycle, and the margin cushions the bank against falling sales or prices.

visual.caption: Bank share = gap x funding rate (for example 75%); the rest is the owner's margin.

regulation.source: A commercial bank's credit procedure manual (2025)
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual sizes working capital need as the working capital to sales ratio times incremental sales, where actual sales are inflated by 35% to 50% depending on capacity utilisation or the sales trend, plus 20% to 25% for cost escalation. Working capital loans must never finance capital items. Repayment is monthly for steady cash flow and may be quarterly for intermittent sectors such as construction and transport.

scenario.title: Financing the whole gap
scenario.situation: Meseret Tadesse, owner of Dire Dawa Spices Trading PLC, shows a projected working capital gap of Birr 8 million and asks for an overdraft of exactly Birr 8 million. She argues that her building is worth Birr 15 million, so the bank is safe.
scenario.question: What should the analyst recommend?
options: Approve Birr 8 million because collateral is ample
Approve Birr 15 million to match the building
Size the limit at a share of the gap, for example Birr 6 million at 75%, with the owner funding the margin
Decline because traders should not use overdrafts
scenario.explain: Collateral is the second way out, not the sizing tool. The owners should fund part of their own trading cycle, which also leaves a cushion if sales or prices fall.

lessons.title: Sizing Bole's overdraft
body: Bole projects FY4 sales of Birr 96 million, with cost of sales at 82% (Birr 78.72 million). The analyst tests two cases: one where the FY3 cycle continues, and one where Bole tightens collections to 45 days and stock to 70 days.

The full Birr 16 million requested fits only if Bole lets its cycle keep stretching, which is the very trend that worries us. A limit of about Birr 15 million, with a condition to bring receivable days to 45 and inventory days to 70, finances real growth without financing slow collections.

worked.title: Bole FY4 overdraft, tightened cycle (Birr thousands)
worked.note: Recommend about Birr 15 million, not 16 million, with a covenant on receivable and inventory days.

scenario.title: The overdraft limit for Bole
scenario.situation: Bole asks to raise its overdraft from Birr 10.5 million to Birr 16 million. Your projection gives a bank share of Birr 18.5 million if the cycle keeps stretching and Birr 15.1 million if Bole tightens to 45 receivable days and 70 inventory days.
scenario.question: Which recommendation is most defensible?
options: Birr 18.5 million, the largest figure the projection supports
About Birr 15 million with a condition to tighten receivable and inventory days
Keep Birr 10.5 million and decline any increase
scenario.explain: Financing the stretched cycle rewards slow collections. About Birr 15 million funds genuine growth, and the condition attacks the root cause. Freezing the limit ignores real sales growth.

lessons.title: The debt service coverage ratio
body: DSCR tests whether operating cash covers the term debt due in a year. In this course: DSCR = (net profit + depreciation + interest on term debt) / (principal due on term debt + interest on term debt). Overdraft interest stays in net profit, because the overdraft is revolving working capital repaid from the trading cycle, not from installments.

A DSCR below 1.0 means the business cannot meet its term debt from operations; the shortfall must come from new borrowing, asset sales or the owners. Many banks look for 1.25 or more to leave a cushion. Test it in each year of the loan, especially the first full repayment year.

visual.caption: Below 1.0: cannot pay from operations. 1.25 or more: a common comfort level.

example.title: Testing a hotel loan year by year
example.text: Lalibela Heritage Lodge PLC asked for a Birr 20 million renovation loan. In year 1, DSCR was 1.6 because principal had a grace period. In year 2, with full principal due, DSCR fell to 1.05. The analyst, Bethlehem Girma, recommended a longer tenor within the asset's useful life so year 2 debt service fell and DSCR rose to 1.3.

lessons.title: Can Bole service the new term loan?
body: Bole's FY4 projection with the packaging line: EBIT margin 7% (EBIT Birr 6,720 thousand), depreciation Birr 1,900 thousand. Debts: overdraft Birr 15,000 thousand at 14%; existing term debt Birr 11,000 thousand at 13% with Birr 2,000 thousand principal due; the new Birr 9,000 thousand loan at 15% over 5 years with equal annual principal. Tax is 30%.

As requested, the loan does not work: FY4 cash covers only 91% of term debt service. A 12-month principal grace on the new loan while the line is installed lifts DSCR to 1.25, with the remaining principal spread over the following years. The analyst must then test year 2, when principal starts; if it fails with realistic margins, the loan is too big for the business.

worked.title: Bole FY4 DSCR as requested (Birr thousands)

rows.label: DSCR with 12-month grace on new principal (5,968 / 4,780)

worked.note: As requested, Bole cannot meet term debt from operations. With grace, it just reaches 1.25.

scenario.title: Fixing a DSCR of 0.91
scenario.situation: Bole's FY4 DSCR on the requested Birr 9 million, 5-year term loan is 0.91. The packaging line will take most of FY4 to install and is expected to lift margins from FY5.
scenario.question: Which structure should the analyst propose?
options: A 12-month principal grace, the balance spread over the following years, plus margin and cycle-day covenants, then test year 2
Approve as requested; collateral covers the shortfall
Shorten the tenor to 3 years to reduce interest
scenario.explain: Grace matches repayment to when the line produces cash, and covenants protect the assumptions. A shorter tenor raises annual principal and makes DSCR worse; collateral is not a repayment source.

lessons.title: Designing repayment, grace and tenor
body: Match the schedule to the cash flow: monthly for steady traders, quarterly or seasonal for agriculture and exporters, a grace period for projects that need time to produce. Grace is on principal; interest is normally still due or collected as the credit decision sets.
Tenor should not exceed the useful life of the asset financed. A loan that outlives its machine leaves the bank financing scrap.

items.label: Short term
items.text: Up to 1 year; grace normally not given, up to 3 months if the business warrants, counted within the tenor

items.label: Medium term
items.text: 13 to 60 months excluding grace; grace typically 6 to 12 months

items.label: Long term
items.text: Over 5 years, typically not above 10 years excluding grace; grace up to 24 months during implementation

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/90/2024 and a commercial bank's credit procedure manual (2025)
regulation.text: A short-term loan has a maximum life of one year under the asset classification and provisioning directive, as the manual cites it. A typical Ethiopian bank manual sets medium-term loans at 13 to 60 months and long-term loans above 5 years, typically up to 10 years, both excluding grace.

example.title: A coffee exporter's seasonal schedule
example.text: Sidama Highland Coffee PLC earns most of its cash from November to March, when washed coffee is shipped. Its analyst, Yonas Tekle, set quarterly installments concentrated in the export season, with a light payment in the rainy months. The same annual principal on a flat monthly schedule would have forced the exporter into overdrafts every August.

lessons.tip: Draw the borrower's monthly cash inflows before choosing the installment frequency.

takeaways: A profitable firm can consume cash: cash from operations deducts the growth in receivables and inventory.
Size the overdraft from the projected working capital gap, with the owner funding a margin; do not finance a stretching cycle.
DSCR below 1.0 means the term debt cannot be paid from operations; many banks look for 1.25 or more.
Test DSCR in each year, especially the first full repayment year, and fix shortfalls with structure, equity or a smaller loan.
Match installments, grace and tenor to the cash flow and keep tenor within the asset's useful life.

quiz.q: Net profit 3,000; depreciation 1,000; receivables up 2,500; inventory up 1,500; payables up 500. Cash flow from operations?
What does a DSCR of 0.8 mean?
options: Operating cash covers only 80% of term debt service
quiz.explain: The 20% shortfall must come from new borrowing, asset sales or the owners.

quiz.q: Why should a bank not finance 100% of the working capital gap?
options: NBE forbids overdrafts above Birr 10 million
The owners need a stake in their trading cycle and the bank needs a cushion
Overdrafts must be fully cash secured
quiz.explain: The margin aligns incentives and absorbs falls in sales or prices.

quiz.q: A coffee exporter earns most of its cash from November to March. How should its term loan be repaid?
options: Quarterly or seasonal installments concentrated in the export season
Interest only for the whole tenor
quiz.explain: Repayment should follow the seasonal cash flow.

quiz.q: Why is overdraft interest left out of the DSCR denominator in this course?
options: The overdraft is revolving working capital repaid from the trading cycle, and its interest is already deducted in net profit
quiz.explain: Only term principal and term interest are in the denominator.

quiz.q: Projected sales Birr 96 million; target receivable days 45. Projected receivables?
quiz.explain: 96,000 x 45 / 365 = about Birr 11,836 thousand.

modules.title: Credit risk grading
modules.summary: Turn judgment into a consistent, documented score that drives approval, collateral, pricing and follow-up intensity.
objectives: Explain why every borrower is graded and when a re-grade is required
Score a borrower on the five-parameter model and its weights
Convert a total score into a grade and a final rating that combines grade with collateral coverage
State what each grade allows, including unsecured lending and the action plan requirement

lessons.title: Why grade every borrower
body: Grading supports the credit decision, flags early warnings, keeps standards uniform across officers, and links to pricing and provisioning. Two officers who rate the same borrower differently are not just disagreeing: they are giving the bank two prices and two collateral demands for the same risk.

In the grading procedure used in this course, all borrowers are graded at every request and reviewed in bulk once a year, and any warning sign triggers an immediate re-grade. New customers and businesses under one year old start at Grade 3. Linked companies (50% common ownership, or first-degree relatives as major shareholders) take the worst grade in the group.

items.label: Decision
items.text: Supports approve, decline or restructure

items.label: Early warning
items.text: A falling score flags trouble before arrears

items.label: Uniformity
items.text: Every officer applies the same yardstick

items.label: Pricing
items.text: Higher risk carries a higher risk premium

items.label: Collateral and follow-up
items.text: Weaker grades need more security and closer monitoring

example.title: Two officers, one borrower
example.text: At a branch in Hawassa, Officer Abebe rated Gedeo Coffee Processing PLC as low risk because he knew the owner well; Officer Saba rated it moderate because the overdraft had not shown a credit balance in eight months. The scoring sheet settled it: account performance pulled the score down to Grade 4. The written evidence, not the relationship, decided the grade.

scenario.title: Sister companies
scenario.situation: Fikru Desta owns 60% of Addis Packaging PLC (Grade 2) and 70% of Addis Transport PLC (Grade 5). Addis Packaging requests a new Birr 7 million term loan.
scenario.question: Which grade applies to the request?
options: Grade 2, the borrowing company's own grade
Grade 5, the worst grade in the linked group
scenario.explain: Companies with 50% or more common ownership are linked, and the linked group takes the worst grade, here Grade 5.

lessons.title: The five parameters and their weights
body: The model scores five parameters, averaged over the latest three years, for a total of 100. Financial risk carries the most weight. It splits into leverage (8), liquidity (8), profitability (7), debt service coverage (6) and quality of statements (6), less 2 or 5 for discrepancies.

Account performance looks at overdraft swing and turnover, term loan repayment, and L/C, merchandise, export and guarantee records. Customer relationship scores length of relationship (6), integrity (6) and borrowing from other banks (3). The manual leaves business and management sub-criteria to the analyst; a workable rubric scores each as strong (80% to 100% of its weight), adequate (55% to 79%) or weak (below 55%), always with written evidence.

visual.caption: Weights of the five parameters, total 100.

regulation.source: A commercial bank's credit procedure manual (2025)
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual requires credit risk grading at the analysis stage on five criteria: account performance and track record, financial soundness, management quality, banking relationship and collateral strength. The grade, the NBE Credit Reference Bureau report and the due diligence report all go into the independent credit analysis.

lessons.tip: Write one line of evidence beside every score. A score without evidence will not survive a committee question.

lessons.title: Scoring the financial parameter
body: Each financial measure has bands by sector. Manufacturing and domestic trade share most bands but differ on leverage and margins, because traders typically run thinner margins and less fixed capital.
Statement quality is scored for exposures of Birr 1 million or more: audited and up to date earns 6, audited plus one year provisional 5, all provisional 3, and a commercial credit report 0.

worked.title: Selected scoring bands

rows.label: Debt / TNW, domestic trade and services

worked.note: Use three-year averages, then apply the discrepancy deduction to the statement score.

scenario.title: A trader's margin
scenario.situation: Bahir Dar General Trading PLC, a domestic trader, has a three-year average operating margin of 5.4% and debt / TNW of 0.9.
scenario.question: What are its profitability and leverage scores?
scenario.explain: For domestic trade, 5% to 5.99% scores 6, and debt / TNW of 0.51 to 1.25 scores 5. A manufacturer with the same margin would score 7.

lessons.title: From score to grade to final rating
body: The total score maps to eight grades. Grades 1 to 3 are bankable, Grade 4 is exceptionally bankable, Grade 5 very exceptionally bankable, and Grades 6 to 8 non-bankable.

The final rating combines the grade with collateral coverage: unsecured, partially secured (below 100%), fully secured (100%) or strongly secured (above 100%), from AAA for bankable and fully secured down to B for non-bankable. Unsecured lending is open only to Grades 1 and 2, and an action plan is required for Grades 3 to 8.

items.label: Grade 1: 85 and above
items.text: Exceptionally low risk, bankable

items.label: Grade 2: 70 to 84
items.text: Very low risk, bankable

items.label: Grade 3: 60 to 69.9
items.text: Low risk, bankable

items.label: Grade 4: 50 to 59.9
items.text: Moderate risk, exceptionally bankable

items.label: Grade 5: 40 to 49.9
items.text: Potential risk, very exceptionally bankable

items.label: Grade 6: 30 to 39.9
items.text: High risk, non-bankable

items.label: Grade 7: 25 to 29.9
items.text: Very high risk, non-bankable

items.label: Grade 8: below 25
items.text: Default, non-bankable

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/90/2024, Asset classification and provisioning
regulation.text: The internal grade is the bank's own judgment; regulatory classification is separate. The directive classifies loans as pass, special mention, substandard, doubtful and loss, with provisions of 1%, 3%, 20%, 50% and 100%, and all non-performing loans go on non-accrual. A falling internal grade is the early warning that should come before a regulatory downgrade.

lessons.title: Demonstration: grading Bole
body: Bole's three-year averages: debt / TNW 1.09, current ratio 1.55, operating margin 7.8%, interest coverage 3.65 times, audited statements with a minor qualification. Business risk is moderate: an essential product, but dependent on imported crude oil and foreign exchange. Management is experienced but has no second line.

Bole scores 79.5: Grade 2, very low risk, bankable. With full collateral cover the final rating is AA. But its falling margins and coverage will cost it points next year if the trend continues, which is why the action plan and covenants matter.

worked.title: Bole Edible Oil: grading score sheet

rows.label: Account performance: average of overdraft 20 and term loan 25
Relationship: 6 years 4, integrity 6, no other bank 3

worked.note: Grade 2 with coverage above 100%: bankable and strongly secured.

example.title: What next year could look like
example.text: The analyst re-ran Bole's sheet with FY3 figures alone: interest coverage 2.6 still scores 6, but if FY4 coverage falls to 2.2, it drops to 5, and a second minor qualification would cut statements again. Two or three such slips would take Bole below 70, to Grade 3, where unsecured lending ends and an action plan becomes mandatory.

lessons.title: Case study: grading Merkato Wholesale
body: Merkato Wholesale PLC (domestic trade, 3 years with the bank) presents only provisional statements for its Birr 6 million exposure. Averages: debt / TNW 2.4, current ratio 1.2, operating margin 3.5%, interest coverage 1.3. One inventory figure differs from VAT records by less than 15% of assets.

Its overdraft runs at 100% of the limit, has not touched credit all year and turns over 1.4 times. A term loan is 20 days in arrears; a previous loan was settled on time but with irregular payments. Integrity is medium and it borrows from two other banks. Assume business 5 and management 8; collateral covers 80% of exposure.

worked.title: Merkato Wholesale: grading score sheet

rows.label: Financial: leverage 0, liquidity 5, margin 3, coverage 3, statements 3, minor discrepancy minus 2
Overdraft: highest debit 7 + no credit balance 4 + turnover 4
Term loan: 1 to 30 days arrears 10 + settled with irregularity 7
Relationship: 3 years 2 + integrity medium 4 + other banks 0

worked.note: Partially secured. No unsecured credit, a mandatory action plan, and any increase declined until leverage and the overdraft swing improve.

scenario.title: Merkato asks for more
scenario.situation: Merkato Wholesale, now graded 47 (Grade 5) with 80% collateral coverage, asks to raise its overdraft from Birr 4 million to Birr 6 million to stock up before a holiday season.
scenario.question: What should the analyst recommend?
options: Approve unsecured, because the season is short
Reclassify Merkato as Grade 3 because it is an existing customer
Decline the increase for now, require an action plan, and revisit when leverage and the overdraft swing improve
scenario.explain: Grade 5 is only very exceptionally bankable, the overdraft is hard-core, and the term loan is in arrears. An action plan comes first; unsecured lending is open only to Grades 1 and 2.

takeaways: Grade every borrower at every request, review all grades yearly and re-grade at once on any warning sign.
Financial risk (35) and account performance (25) carry the most weight; every score needs written evidence.
New customers start at Grade 3, and a linked group takes its worst member's grade.
Grades 1 to 3 are bankable; only Grades 1 and 2 may borrow unsecured; Grades 3 to 8 need an action plan.
The internal grade is separate from NBE classification, but a falling grade is the early warning before a regulatory downgrade.

quiz.q: What grade does a brand-new customer start at?
quiz.explain: New customers and businesses under one year old start at Grade 3.

quiz.q: Which parameter carries the most weight?
quiz.explain: Financial risk carries 35 of the 100 points.

quiz.q: A borrower scores 58. What grade, and is it bankable?
options: Grade 4, moderate risk, exceptionally bankable only
quiz.explain: 50 to 59.9 is Grade 4, moderate risk, exceptionally bankable.

quiz.q: Two sister companies are Grades 2 and 5. Which grade applies to the group's request?
quiz.explain: Linked companies take the worst grade in the group.

quiz.q: Which grades may receive unsecured loans?
quiz.explain: Unsecured lending is open only to Grades 1 and 2.

quiz.q: A manufacturer's three-year average debt / TNW is 1.09. What leverage score?
quiz.explain: For manufacturing, 0.76 to 1.25 scores 5.

modules.title: Structuring and pricing the facility
modules.summary: Shape security, the owner's stake, conditions and price so that the deal fits the risk the analysis has found.
objectives: Compute collateral coverage after haircuts and apply revaluation rules
Set and verify the owner's equity contribution for project, vehicle and machinery loans
Draft conditions precedent and financial, information and operating covenants
Build a loan price from cost of funds, operating cost, margin, term premium and risk premium

lessons.title: Collateral coverage and haircuts
body: Collateral coverage = acceptable collateral value after haircuts / total exposure. Haircuts reflect what the bank would actually recover in a forced sale, after time, costs and depreciation.

In the manuals used in this course, used vehicles and machinery count at 90%, 75% or 50% of the lower of invoice or insurance value depending on age (for example a 2-year-old vehicle at 90%, a 4-year-old truck at 75%, machinery 5 to 7 years old at 50%). Cash deposits, treasury bills and bank guarantees must cover at least 85% of the loan; shares of banks and insurers count at up to 80% to 90% of the lower of par or market; merchandise at 70% to 90% of the lower of cost or market.

visual.caption: Below 100%: partially secured. 100%: fully secured. Above 100%: strongly secured.

rows.label: Trucks, 4 years old, insurance value 6.0 at 75%

regulation.source: Movable Property Security Right Proclamation No. 1147/2019 and NBE Directive No. MCR/01/2020
regulation.text: Movables such as inventories, vehicles, machinery, business mortgages, shares and cash collateral can secure a loan and are registered on the Ethiopian Movable Collateral Registry. A typical Ethiopian bank manual adds that the bank, never the borrower, registers the collateral, and that property held in a trade name cannot be collateral.

lessons.title: Collateral types and their rules
body: Each collateral type has its own valuation basis and risks. Buildings are valued by a bank engineer or an accepted independent valuer; the estimation fee is borne by the borrower. Revaluation keeps values honest: manuals differ, one revaluing buildings every 2 years and another every 3, with machinery and vehicles revalued every 2 years and depreciated at least 10% a year.

A typical Ethiopian bank manual does not accept vehicles or construction machinery more than 10 years from manufacture (10 to 15 years only exceptionally), accepts vehicles for an overdraft only together with a building, and refrains from second-degree mortgages unless there is a clear margin over the first loan.

items.label: Buildings
items.text: Engineer's valuation; under construction at least 60% (residential) or 65% (commercial) complete

items.label: Vehicles and machinery
items.text: Lower of insurance, assessor or market value; new at invoice; age limits apply

items.label: Merchandise
items.text: Lower of cost or market; pledged and insured against fire and burglary

items.label: Cash and T-bills
items.text: Blocked with a letter of assignment; maturities matched to the loan

items.label: Shares
items.text: Credible companies only, transfer undertaking from the issuer; never the bank's own shares

items.label: Personal guarantees
items.text: Treated as clean (unsecured) loans

example.title: A building in a trade name
example.text: Wondimu Tefera offered a warehouse in Kality as collateral, but the title was registered under his shop's trade name, "Wondimu Hardware", not under his own name or a company. The analyst explained that trade-name property is not acceptable. Wondimu transferred the title to his PLC, the bank engineer revalued it, and the mortgage was registered two weeks later.

lessons.tip: Diary the revaluation date of every collateral item when you book it; stale values are the most common audit finding.

lessons.title: The owner's equity contribution
body: The owner's own money keeps their incentives aligned with the bank's. The manuals require at least 30% of project cost for medium and long-term project loans, never from borrowed money; 30% for vehicle loans (60% removes the need for extra collateral); 30% or 35% for construction machinery depending on grade, plus extra building collateral; and 20% to 40% for home loans.

Verify the source of equity from bank statements and the credit report, and block it in an account before disbursement. Borrowed equity puts no owner money at risk and adds hidden debt that competes for the same cash flow.

scenario.title: Equity from a relative's loan
scenario.situation: Kalkidan Mesfin needs 30% equity, Birr 2.4 million, for a new Birr 8 million bakery line. Her bank statements show the Birr 2.4 million arrived last week from her brother, with a signed note that she will repay him over two years.
scenario.question: How should the analyst treat this contribution?
options: Treat it as borrowed money: it is not equity, so require genuine owner funds or reduce the project
Accept it; the money is in her account
Accept it if the brother signs as guarantor
Accept half of it as equity
scenario.explain: Equity must not come from borrowed money. The note to her brother is debt competing for the bakery's cash flow, so it does not put owner money at risk.

example.title: Blocking equity before disbursement
example.text: For a Birr 14 million cold-store project in Mojo, Hailu Agro Exports PLC contributed Birr 4.2 million (30%). The analyst traced the funds to two years of retained profits in the company's account, confirmed the credit report showed no new borrowing, and required the Birr 4.2 million to be blocked and paid to the contractor first, before any bank money moved.

lessons.title: Conditions precedent and covenants
body: Conditions precedent must be met before any disbursement. Covenants keep the risk where it was approved for the life of the loan. Good covenants are specific, measurable and tied to the risks the analysis found.

For Bole the analyst proposed: debt / TNW not above 1.5; current ratio not below 1.3; receivable days 45 or less by FY4 year end; at least 70% of sales routed through the bank; no dividend while DSCR is below 1.25; audited statements within 4 months of year end; no new borrowing elsewhere without consent.

items.label: Conditions precedent
items.text: Equity blocked, contracts signed and registered, insurance endorsed, supplier contract presented

items.label: Financial covenants
items.text: Maximum leverage, minimum current ratio or DSCR, limits on dividends and new borrowing

items.label: Information covenants
items.text: Audited statements within a set time; an annual business performance report for large exposures

items.label: Operating covenants
items.text: Route sales through the bank, keep collateral insured, no ownership change without consent

scenario.title: A dividend request
scenario.situation: Six months after approval, Bole's board wants to pay a Birr 1 million dividend. The latest management accounts show a DSCR of 1.1 and receivable days of 52.
scenario.question: What does the covenant package allow?
options: The dividend, because profit is positive
The dividend if Bole adds collateral
Half the dividend now and half later
No dividend while DSCR is below 1.25; also raise the receivable days breach with management
scenario.explain: The covenant blocks dividends while DSCR is below 1.25, and receivable days above 45 is a second warning that needs an action plan.

lessons.title: Pricing to the risk
body: A sound lending rate covers the cost of funds, a reasonable spread for operating cost, a return on capital and a mark-up for credit risk, with medium-term loans priced above short-term and long-term above medium-term. Longer loans carry more uncertainty, tie up funds longer and create a maturity mismatch against mostly short-term deposits.

The risk premium approximates expected loss: probability of default (PD) x loss given default (LGD). Fees complete the price: processing and valuation fees, a commitment fee on undisbursed project loans, guarantee commissions and a redemption fee on early full repayment.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. NBE/INT/13/2026, Interest rates (as amended)
regulation.text: Each bank freely sets its lending rates. Rates must be approved in writing by the bank's board, based on explicit written criteria, and reported to the NBE. A transparent build-up such as this one is how an analyst shows that a price follows the bank's approved criteria.

worked.title: Bole's price build-up: overdraft, 5-year term loan

rows.label: Risk premium, Grade 2: PD 1.5% x LGD 35%

worked.note: Merkato Wholesale (Grade 5, PD about 8%, LGD 45%) would carry a 3.6% risk premium, an overdraft rate of about 17.1%, and only if the bank lends at all.

scenario.title: Pricing a weaker borrower
scenario.situation: A borrower has PD 4% and LGD 50%. Cost of funds is 7.5%, operating cost 3%, target margin 3%, and the facility is a 1-year overdraft with no term premium.
scenario.question: What rate does the build-up give?

lessons.title: Demonstration: Bole's package
body: The packaging line costs Birr 12,900 thousand. Bole contributes Birr 3,900 thousand (30.2%) into a blocked account; the bank lends Birr 9,000 thousand, paid directly to the supplier. The overdraft is set at Birr 15,000 thousand from the working capital analysis.

Total exposure is 15,000 + 9,000 + 11,000 existing = Birr 35,000 thousand. Collateral after haircuts is Birr 46,900 thousand, so coverage is 134%: strongly secured, which with Grade 2 gives the AA rating.

rows.label: Factory land and building, bank engineer's valuation
Existing machinery, 5 to 7 years old: 50% of insurance value 8,000
New packaging line at invoice value

example.title: Same borrower, two structures
example.text: Structure A gave Bole Birr 16 million of overdraft and a Birr 9 million, 5-year loan with no grace and no covenants. Structure B gave Birr 15 million with cycle-day conditions, a 12-month grace, blocked equity, payment to the supplier and seven covenants. Both had the same collateral. The committee approved B, because it fixed the two risks the analysis found: slow collections and thin FY4 cash flow.

lessons.title: Case study: Abay Construction's excavator
body: Abay Construction PLC (Grade 3) wants a new excavator for Birr 10,000,000. It can contribute 40% and offers a building valued at Birr 2,400,000. Under the manual used in this case, a Grade 3 customer must contribute at least 35% and add a building worth at least 45% of the loan; at 65% equity no extra collateral is needed; between the two, extra collateral is reduced proportionately.

Reading "proportionately" as a straight line from 45% at 35% equity to 0% at 65% equity, the requirement at 40% equity is 37.5% of the loan. Teams must state that this interpretation needs confirmation from the credit department before relying on it.

worked.title: Abay Construction: equity and building required

items.label: Block equity
items.text: Birr 4,000,000 in a blocked account

items.label: Supplier documents
items.text: Supplier contract and final invoice; confirm the machine is new

items.label: Ownership and pledge
items.text: Transfer to Abay, pledge to the bank, register with the designated ministry

items.label: Insurance
items.text: Contractor's all risks, fire and theft, naming the bank first

items.label: Mortgage
items.text: Register the building mortgage

items.label: Pay
items.text: Disburse directly to the supplier

scenario.title: Equity versus building
scenario.situation: Abay can contribute 40% equity and offers a Birr 2.4 million building. At 35% equity the building requirement would be Birr 2.925 million.
scenario.question: What is the best recommendation?
options: Lend at 35% equity, since the building is close enough
Lend Birr 6 million at 40% equity, subject to credit department confirmation of the proportional reading
Decline, because Grade 3 cannot borrow for machinery
scenario.explain: At 40% equity the straight-line requirement is Birr 2.25 million, which the building meets. The reading of "proportionately" must be confirmed, so the recommendation says so.

takeaways: Coverage is collateral after haircuts divided by total exposure; haircuts reflect what the bank would really recover.
Revalue collateral on schedule and respect age limits; the bank, not the borrower, registers the collateral.
Equity must be the owner's own money, traced and blocked before disbursement.
Conditions precedent protect disbursement; financial, information and operating covenants protect the life of the loan.
Price = cost of funds + operating cost + target margin + term premium + risk premium (PD x LGD), set within board-approved criteria.

quiz.q: Exposure Birr 20 million; building Birr 18 million; 4-year-old trucks with insurance value Birr 6 million counted at 75%. Coverage?
Why must the equity contribution not come from borrowed money?
options: It puts no owner money at risk and adds hidden debt competing for the same cash flow
quiz.explain: Borrowed equity breaks the alignment that equity is meant to create.

quiz.q: Which is an information covenant?
options: Route 70% of sales through the bank
Audited statements within 4 months of year end
quiz.explain: Information covenants require reports and statements on time.

quiz.q: A loan has PD 4% and LGD 50%. What risk premium is implied?
How should a 7-year loan be priced relative to a 3-year loan?
options: Lower, as the bank earns interest longer
Higher, because long-term loans carry more uncertainty and a term premium
quiz.explain: Long-term loans are priced above medium-term loans.

quiz.q: Under the NBE interest rate directive, who must approve a bank's lending rates?
options: The bank's board, in writing, on explicit criteria, reported to the NBE
quiz.explain: Banks set rates freely within board-approved written criteria and report them to the NBE.

modules.title: Account performance, the credit report and the committee
modules.summary: Pull the analysis into one written recommendation and defend it before a credit committee that asks hard questions.
objectives: Measure account performance across overdraft, merchandise, L/C, pre-shipment, guarantee and term loan facilities
Write a credit analysis report in the standard eleven-section format
Draft a one-page executive summary that states a clear recommendation, the key risk and its mitigant
Defend a recommendation under committee questioning, including sensitivity and policy exceptions

lessons.title: Reading account performance
body: Account conduct is the borrower's track record in the bank's own books: hard evidence that no statement can dress up. Each facility has its own measures and healthy signs.

Watch for facilities settled by conversion into another loan, by selling collateral or by buyout from another bank: the grading model used in this course deducts 5 to 10 points for each. A loan that was "repaid" with another loan was not repaid.

worked.title: Healthy signs by facility (from the manuals)

rows.label: Overdraft
rows.value: Highest debit above 85% of limit, credit balance within 3 months, turnover above 3 times

rows.label: Merchandise loan
rows.value: Turnover above 3 times; advances settled within 90 days (180 for coffee)

rows.label: Import L/C facility
rows.value: Documents settled within a week; turnover above 3 times

rows.label: Pre-shipment advance
rows.value: Turnover above 4 times; settled within 5 days of shipment

rows.label: Term loan
rows.value: Paid regularly; past loans settled on schedule

regulation.source: A commercial bank's credit procedure manual (2025), citing NBE Directive No. SBB/90/2024
regulation.text: An overdraft is reviewed and renewed at least every year. A typical Ethiopian bank manual rates turnover above 4 times as excellent and 1 time or less as poor, and swing (highest debit as a share of the limit) above 85% as excellent and below 40% as poor. An overdraft with unsatisfactory turnover or swing may be called back or converted, in full or in part, into a term loan.

left.title: A healthy overdraft
items: Used actively up to the limit

right.title: A hard-core overdraft
items: Sits at the limit all year

lessons.title: When an overdraft goes hard-core
body: An overdraft that never swings into credit has become permanent finance, usually for a long-term need such as unpaid receivables or fixed assets bought with working capital. Its interest is capitalised at month end, so the balance can quietly grow.

The remedies are to call the facility back, reduce the limit, convert all or part into a term loan with a proper schedule, or require additional security. The analyst first asks why the money is stuck, because the remedy must fit the cause.

scenario.title: An overdraft that never swings
scenario.situation: Kidus Furniture PLC's Birr 5 million overdraft has not shown a credit balance in 14 months and total credits were Birr 4.5 million over the year, a turnover of 0.9 times. The owner, Kidist Abera, says she used part of the line to buy a new CNC machine.
scenario.question: Which response best fits the cause?
options: Renew at the same limit and wait
Convert the machine-related part into a term loan with a schedule, reduce the overdraft limit, and seek additional security if coverage is short
Increase the limit so the account can swing
Report the account as a loss immediately
scenario.explain: Working capital lines must not finance capital items. Converting that portion to a term loan matches the asset, and a reduced limit restores a working overdraft.

example.title: Turning a stuck line around
example.text: Debre Birhan Malt Supplies PLC had a Birr 8 million overdraft frozen at the limit. The analyst, Rahel Kassahun, found Birr 3 million was tied up in a delayed payment from a brewery. The bank converted Birr 3 million into a 24-month term loan, cut the overdraft to Birr 5 million and required the brewery's payments to be routed through the account. Within two quarters the overdraft turned over 3.2 times.

lessons.title: The credit analysis report
body: The report follows the bank's format so every committee sees the same issues in the same order, and it covers both financial and non-financial risks. For an existing customer like Bole, focus on what has changed since the last approval.

The compliance section is where the analyst confirms single borrower and related party limits and names any policy exception and who must approve it. A report that hides an exception is worse than a report that declines.

items.label: Executive summary
items.text: Request, recommendation, amount, tenor, price, conditions, grade, coverage

items.label: Background
items.text: Ownership, management, history, group exposure, relationship

items.label: Purpose and justification
items.text: What the money pays for, why this product and tenor

items.label: Industry and market
items.text: Outlook, competition, supply, foreign exchange, regulation

items.label: Financial analysis
items.text: Spreads, ratio trends, cash flow, working capital, projections

items.label: Repayment capacity
items.text: DSCR by year and sensitivity

items.label: Account performance and credit report
items.text: Own books and the NBE Credit Reference Bureau

items.label: Collateral
items.text: Valuation, haircut, ownership, defects, insurance, coverage

items.label: Risk grade and key risks
items.text: With a mitigant for each

items.label: Compliance
items.text: Single borrower and related party limits, exceptions

items.label: Terms and conditions
items.text: Conditions precedent, covenants, disbursement, repayment

regulation.source: NBE Directives No. SBB/87/2024 (Large exposures) and No. SBB/88/2024 (Related party transactions)
regulation.text: A large exposure is 10% or more of the bank's total capital, and exposure to one counterparty group may not exceed 25% of total capital. Related party exposure is limited to 15% per related party and 35% in aggregate, on arm's-length terms, with board approval above Birr 15 million. The compliance section of the report confirms both.

worked.title: Checking Bank A's large exposure limit (illustrative, Birr millions)

rows.label: Share of total capital
rows.value: 0.9%: well within limits, not a large exposure

lessons.title: A weak and a strong executive summary
body: The executive summary is often the only page every committee member reads closely. It must state a clear recommendation, which may differ from the request, the numbers behind it, the key risk and the mitigant tied to it.
Compare the two versions for Bole. The weak one could describe any borrower. The strong one could describe only Bole.

left.title: Weak
items: "A well-known and reputable company with good collateral."
"We recommend approval as it will generate income for the bank."
No numbers, no risk, no conditions

right.title: Strong
items: Overdraft Birr 10.5 to 15 million (not 16) for 12 months at 14%
Birr 9 million, 6-year term loan, 12 months' grace, 15%, paid to the supplier after Birr 3.9 million equity is blocked
Key risk: falling margins; FY4 DSCR 1.25 only with grace; covenants cap leverage at 1.5 and receivable days at 45

example.title: The analyst rewrites a summary
example.text: Samuel Getachew's first draft for Ambo Mineral Water PLC said "strong customer, adequate security". His team leader sent it back. The second draft read: "We recommend a Birr 12 million, 5-year bottling line loan at 15% with 6 months' grace; Grade 3 (64); coverage 118%; key risk is a new competitor in Oromia, mitigated by a three-year supply contract with a distributor covering 40% of volume." The committee approved it in ten minutes.

lessons.tip: If your summary does not contain at least five numbers and one named risk, rewrite it.

lessons.title: Facing the committee
body: In the capstone, teams of four play the presenting analyst, the branch manager and two probing committee members. Each team presents its Bole recommendation in 7 minutes and takes 8 minutes of questions; the chair records the decision on a mock loan approval form with reasons.
Scoring is out of 20: quality of analysis 6, soundness of structure 5, handling of questions 5, completeness of conditions 4. Prepare for the hard questions before you walk in.
points: Why should we finance slower collections from Bole's customers?
What happens to DSCR if crude oil prices rise another 10% and the margin falls to 5%?
Who would run the business if the founder left?
Is any part of this an exception to policy, and who must approve it?
How will we know within 3 months whether the covenants are being met?

worked.title: Sensitivity: Bole FY4 with EBIT margin at 5% (Birr thousands)
worked.note: If the margin falls to 5%, Bole cannot meet term debt even with the grace period. The answer to the committee: the margin covenant and quarterly monitoring are the early warning, and the owners must stand ready to inject funds.

scenario.title: The sensitivity question
scenario.situation: A committee member asks what happens if Bole's EBIT margin falls from 7% to 5% in FY4. Your sensitivity shows DSCR falling from 1.25 to 0.96 even with the 12-month grace.
scenario.question: What is the most credible answer?
options: Say the scenario is unlikely and move on
Acknowledge the 0.96, then explain the margin covenant, quarterly monitoring, and an owner support commitment or a smaller loan as mitigants
Point out that collateral coverage is 134%, so DSCR does not matter
scenario.explain: Committees trust analysts who show the downside and how it is controlled. Collateral is the second way out, not a substitute for repayment capacity.

lessons.title: After the decision: notification to disbursement
body: Approval is not the end of the analyst's work. The decision is communicated in writing with every condition stated. Before disbursement the bank checks that contracts are signed and registered, collateral is insured with the policy endorsed to the bank, and all conditions precedent, charges and stamp duty are met.

A typical Ethiopian bank manual requires disbursement within 90 days of approval (180 days where the bank pays a seller for an asset), or the loan returns for re-approval. After disbursement, follow-up visits verify end use, and any warning sign triggers a re-grade.

items.label: Decision
items.text: Written notification stating all conditions

items.label: Documentation
items.text: Loan and mortgage contracts signed with two witnesses; bank registers collateral

items.label: Conditions precedent
items.text: Equity blocked, insurance endorsed, stamp duty and charges paid

items.label: Disbursement
items.text: Within 90 days (180 for asset purchases); paid to the supplier where possible

items.label: Follow-up
items.text: End-use visit, covenant checks, annual review and re-grade on warning signs

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. CRB/02/2019, Credit Reference Bureau (as cited in a commercial bank's credit manual)
regulation.text: Credit information is pulled from the NBE Credit Reference Bureau for new loans, renewals, rescheduling, collateral release and refinancing, with the written consent of the borrower and guarantors. A typical Ethiopian bank manual also checks persons related to the borrower.

scenario.title: An approval about to lapse
scenario.situation: Bole's package was approved 85 days ago, but the packaging line supplier has not yet issued the final invoice and the equity is still not blocked.
scenario.question: What should the analyst do?
options: Disburse the term loan now to beat the deadline
Disburse to Bole's current account and collect the invoice later
Note that payment to a seller for an asset allows up to 180 days, keep all conditions precedent, and track the new deadline
scenario.explain: Where the bank pays the seller for an asset acquisition, the validity in the manual is 180 days. Conditions precedent are never waived to meet a date.

takeaways: Account conduct in the bank's own books is hard evidence; conversions, collateral sales and buyouts are not true repayment.
A hard-core overdraft needs a remedy that fits its cause: reduce, convert, call back or secure.
The credit report follows one format so every committee sees every risk, including compliance with large exposure and related party limits.
A strong executive summary gives the recommendation, the numbers, the key risk and the mitigant on one page.
Show the committee the downside sensitivity and how covenants and monitoring will catch it early.

quiz.q: An overdraft never shows a credit balance and turns over 0.9 times. Which is an appropriate remedy?
options: Convert all or part into a term loan or reduce the limit
quiz.explain: Call back, reduce the limit, convert to a term loan or require additional security.

quiz.q: What is a condition precedent?
options: A condition that must be met before any disbursement, such as registering the mortgage
quiz.explain: Conditions precedent come before the money moves.

quiz.q: Which healthy sign applies to a pre-shipment advance?
options: Turnover above 4 times and settled within 5 days of shipment
quiz.explain: Pre-shipment advances should turn over quickly and settle soon after shipment.

quiz.q: Under SBB/87/2024, exposure to one counterparty group may not exceed:
quiz.explain: 25% is the single-group limit; 10% defines a large exposure.

quiz.q: What most distinguishes a strong executive summary?
options: A clear recommendation with numbers, the key risk and its mitigant
A list of all documents received
quiz.explain: Committees need a decision-ready page.

quiz.q: In this course's grading model, how is a facility settled by selling collateral treated?
options: As a deduction of 5 to 10 points
quiz.explain: Settlement by conversion, collateral sale or buyout costs 5 to 10 points each.

simulation.title: A week as credit analyst at Bank A, Adama branch
setting: You have just joined the credit desk of Bank A's Adama branch, a busy trade and agro-processing hub on the Addis to Djibouti corridor. The branch has a loan book of about Birr 900 million, mostly overdrafts, merchandise loans and term loans to small and medium manufacturers and traders.

Your job this week: analyse every request that reaches the desk, recommend a decision and a structure, and protect the bank's portfolio without losing good customers. The branch manager and the district credit committee rely on your work. Every item comes in the order it reaches you, and each decision has consequences later in the week.
Work it as you would on the job: read the facts, do the numbers on paper or a spreadsheet, and choose the action you would defend in front of the committee and the NBE examiner.

authority.title: Your desk's rules and targets

rows.label: Overdraft sizing
rows.value: Up to 75% of the working capital gap (bank's teaching rule)

rows.label: Term loans
rows.value: DSCR of 1.25 or more in every year; tenor within the asset's useful life

rows.label: Unsecured lending
rows.value: Grades 1 and 2 only; action plan for Grades 3 to 8

rows.label: Vehicles and machinery
rows.value: Not accepted more than 10 years from manufacture

rows.label: Pricing
rows.value: Board-approved written criteria; exceptions approved in writing

rows.label: Bank A total capital
rows.value: Birr 4,000 million; related party limit 15% per party, board approval above Birr 15 million

rows.label: Disbursement
rows.value: Within 90 days of approval (180 days for asset purchases), or back for re-approval

authority.note: These follow the course and a typical Ethiopian bank manual. Your own bank's policy always comes first.

meters.label: Portfolio quality
meters.help: Rises with sound analysis and structure; falls when risk is approved without being understood.

meters.label: Customer relationships
meters.help: Rises when good customers are served well and quickly; falls with needless refusals or delays.

meters.label: Compliance
meters.help: Falls sharply with any breach of NBE directives or the bank's policy, hidden or not.

meters.label: Branch income
meters.help: Rises with well-priced business; falls with underpriced loans and losses.

tasks.subject: New customer: Adama Flour Mill PLC, Birr 12 million overdraft, urgent
body: Great news: Adama Flour Mill PLC wants to move its banking to us. Sales grew 40% in two years, from Birr 51 million to Birr 72 million. They need a Birr 12 million overdraft before the harvest season. The owner is well known in town and other banks are chasing him. Can we get this to committee by Wednesday?

Attached: three years of statements. Your quick look shows receivable days rising from 48 to 95 and the operating margin falling from 8% to 5%. The latest audit opinion is qualified: the auditor could not observe the year-end stock count.

options.text: Back the growth story and fast-track the application: the owner is reputable and competitors are waiting.
options.outcome: The application moves fast, but nobody asked why the cash is stuck in receivables or what the qualified opinion hides. Growth funded by slow collections is the classic trap from Module 1.

options.text: Spread the statements, work out the cash conversion cycle and ask the customer about the slower collections and the qualified stock count before sizing anything.
options.outcome: Right order. Spreading shows that most of the new money would finance slower collections, and the qualification needs an answer before stock can be relied on. You can still meet the RM's timetable with a better-founded proposal.

options.text: Decline straight away: a qualified audit opinion rules the company out.
options.outcome: Too blunt. A qualification is a question to resolve, not an automatic refusal; the grading model deducts points for it. You lose a potentially sound customer without analysing the business.

options.text: Ask for a building as collateral first; if it covers the limit, the analysis can be light.
options.outcome: Collateral is the second way out, never the first. A loan that can only be repaid by selling the building is a bad loan, whatever it is secured on.

tasks.subject: Sizing the overdraft for Adama Flour Mill
body: The customer explains that two large distributors paid late last year; both have now agreed 45-day terms. The auditor confirms the stock count issue was a timing problem and has re-counted. The customer still asks for Birr 12 million.
Next year's plan: sales of Birr 72 million, cost of sales at 80%. Target cycle agreed with the customer: receivables 45 days, inventory 60 days, payables 30 days.

exhibit.title: Inputs for the working capital gap (Birr thousands)

options.text: Birr 12 million, as requested: the business is growing.
options.outcome: The gap is 8,877 + 9,468 minus 4,734 = Birr 13,611 thousand, and 75% of it is about Birr 10.2 million. Birr 12 million would fund the slow collections you were told have been fixed, with no owner margin left.

options.text: About Birr 10.2 million, with covenants holding receivables to 45 days and inventory to 60 days.
options.outcome: Correct: receivables 72,000 x 45 / 365 = 8,877, inventory 57,600 x 60 / 365 = 9,468, payables 57,600 x 30 / 365 = 4,734, gap 13,611, bank share 75% = 10,208. The covenants keep the cycle where the limit assumes it is.

options.text: Birr 13.6 million, the full working capital gap.
options.outcome: Funding 100% of the gap leaves the owners with no stake in their own trading cycle and the bank with no cushion if sales or prices fall. The owner's margin is a basic rule from Module 2.

options.text: Birr 6 million to be safe, and review in a year.
options.outcome: Under-lending is also a risk: a mill that cannot buy wheat at harvest misses sales, stretches suppliers and may end up borrowing elsewhere. Size to the need, then control it with covenants.

tasks.subject: Birr 6 million, 4-year term loan for a carton machine
body: Wonji Packaging, a customer for five years with a clean record, wants a Birr 6 million term loan over 4 years, with equal annual principal, to buy a carton-making machine with a useful life of 7 years. The machine takes about 9 months to install and run in. The owner offers a building worth Birr 9 million as collateral.
You projected the first year with the new loan.

exhibit.title: Wonji Packaging, first year with the new loan (Birr thousands)

options.text: Approve as requested: the building covers 150% of the loan.
options.outcome: DSCR = (1,500 + 700 + 900) / (2,500 + 900) = 3,100 / 3,400 = 0.91. The business cannot pay this schedule from operations in year one. Collateral does not change that; it only tells you what you lose if it fails.

options.text: Restructure: 12 months' grace on the new principal while the machine is installed, then test year 2, when principal starts.
options.outcome: With grace, year-one service is 1,000 + 900 = 1,900 and DSCR = 3,100 / 1,900 = 1.63. Grace matches repayment to when the machine earns. You still owe the committee the year-2 test with realistic margins.

options.text: Stretch the tenor to 10 years so the installments fall.
options.outcome: The machine lasts 7 years. A loan that outlives its asset leaves the bank financing scrap in the last years. Fix the timing with grace, not with a tenor longer than the asset's life.

options.text: Decline: a DSCR below 1.0 means the loan cannot work.
options.outcome: The ratio is below 1.0 only because principal falls due before the machine produces. A good analyst redesigns the repayment before declining a sound customer.

tasks.from: Bole Edible Oil PLC, general manager
tasks.subject: Renew and raise our overdraft to Birr 16 million
body: Bole's overdraft of Birr 10.5 million is due for its annual renewal. The general manager asks to raise it to Birr 16 million and says business is booming.

The account statement for the last 12 months shows the balance never below Birr 9.8 million and never in credit. Credit turnover was 0.9 times the limit. Interest has been capitalised every month. Two months ago Bole paid for a new filling machine from the overdraft.
tasks.ask: What do you propose at renewal?

options.text: Renew and raise to Birr 16 million: Bole is a six-year customer.
options.outcome: The overdraft is hard-core: it never swings and turns over less than once, so it is financing fixed assets and slow receivables. Raising it adds to the problem the account is already showing.

options.text: Find out why the money is stuck, convert the hard-core part, including the machine, into a term loan with a schedule, and renew a smaller revolving limit sized on the cycle.
options.outcome: The remedy fits the cause: the machine belongs on a term loan, and the revolving limit goes back to financing the trading cycle. Turnover of 1 time or less is poor under a typical manual, and conversion is one of the standard remedies.

options.text: Call back the whole overdraft now.
options.outcome: Calling the full balance from a going concern that cannot repay at once pushes it into default. Calling back is a remedy of last resort, used after the cause is understood.

options.text: Renew unchanged for another year and look again then.
options.outcome: Renewing a hard-core overdraft unchanged lets the balance keep growing with capitalised interest. The annual review exists to catch exactly this.

tasks.subject: Unsecured overdraft for Nazret Transport S.C.
body: Your grading of Nazret Transport S.C. comes out at Grade 4, exceptionally bankable: strong account conduct but high leverage and weak management depth. The branch manager writes: 'The chairman is an important person in town. Propose a Birr 3 million unsecured overdraft; we can't ask him for collateral.'

options.text: Propose it unsecured as asked.
options.outcome: Unsecured lending is open only to Grades 1 and 2. Proposing it for a Grade 4 borrower is a policy breach that you, as the analyst, would be signing.

options.text: Re-score management as 'strong' so the grade improves to 2.
options.outcome: Changing a score without written evidence to reach a wanted answer is manipulating the grading. It is exactly what internal audit and NBE examiners look for.

options.text: Propose a secured facility with an action plan for Grade 4, and explain the rule to the branch manager in writing.
options.outcome: You keep the customer within policy. Grades 3 to 8 need an action plan, and the written note protects both you and the branch manager.

options.text: Decline the application.
options.outcome: Grade 4 is bankable as an exception, with security and an action plan. Declining loses a customer the bank could serve safely.

tasks.subject: Collateral coverage for a Birr 20 million package
body: Please confirm the collateral coverage for Metehara Logistics PLC's Birr 20 million total exposure. Offered: a warehouse, valued by the bank engineer at Birr 15 million; Truck A, 4 years old, insurance value Birr 8 million; Truck B, manufactured 12 years ago, insurance value Birr 3 million.

rows.label: Vehicles about 2 years old
rows.value: 90% of the lower of invoice or insurance value

options.text: Birr 26 million, 130%: count everything at its value.
options.outcome: Collateral counts at what the bank would recover in a forced sale. Ignoring haircuts and the age limit overstates your protection by Birr 5 million.

options.text: Birr 21 million, 105%: the warehouse plus Truck A at 75%; Truck B is not acceptable.
options.outcome: Correct: 15 + (8 x 75%) = 21, and 21 / 20 = 105%, strongly secured. Truck B is past the 10-year limit, so it does not count.

options.text: Birr 22.5 million, 112.5%: Truck B at 50% as old machinery.
options.outcome: Truck B is a vehicle more than 10 years from manufacture: the manual does not accept it at all, so no haircut makes it eligible.

options.text: Birr 15 million, 75%: only buildings count, so ask for more collateral.
options.outcome: Vehicles are acceptable movable collateral when registered and within the age limit. Ignoring Truck A understates coverage and sends the customer looking for collateral it does not need.

tasks.subject: Match a competitor's 13% for Merkato Wholesale
body: Merkato Wholesale, graded 5 (very exceptionally bankable), wants a Birr 5 million overdraft. Another bank has offered 13%. The RM asks you to price at 13% to win the account.
Your bank's approved build-up: cost of funds 7.5%, operating cost 3.0%, target margin 3.0%, risk premium = probability of default x loss given default. For Merkato, PD is about 8% and LGD about 45%.
tasks.ask: What price do you put in the proposal?

options.text: 13%, to win the customer.
options.outcome: The risk premium alone is 8% x 45% = 3.6%, so the rate that covers costs and risk is 7.5 + 3.0 + 3.0 + 3.6 = 17.1%. At 13% the bank loses money on a risky customer, outside its board-approved criteria.

options.text: About 17.1%, following the approved criteria, or decline if the customer will not pay for its risk.
options.outcome: Rates must follow the board's written criteria, which are reported to the NBE. A Grade 5 borrower that only stays at 13% is a customer another bank is underpricing, not one to chase.

options.text: 15% as a 'relationship rate', agreed verbally with the RM.
options.outcome: Any exception must be approved in writing by whoever holds that authority. A verbal discount is still underpricing, and now it is undocumented.

options.text: 13% on paper, with extra service fees to make up the difference.
options.outcome: Hiding the real price in fees misleads the customer and breaks transparency rules on charges. If it surfaces, it costs the bank its reputation as well.

tasks.from: Assistant to a member of the board
