tasks.subject: Birr 70 million overdraft for Gara Mulata Trading
body: Gara Mulata Trading S.C., in which one of Bank A's directors holds 30%, applies for a Birr 70 million overdraft. The director's assistant writes: 'Please process quickly and at a preferential rate. If board approval is a problem, it could be arranged as five loans of Birr 14 million.'
Bank A's total capital is Birr 4,000 million.

options.text: Process at the preferential rate as a courtesy to the director.
options.outcome: Related party credit must be on arm's-length terms: the same rate and conditions as any other customer. A preferential rate is exactly the abuse the related party directive prevents.

options.text: Split it into five loans of Birr 14 million, each below the board approval threshold.
options.outcome: Splitting to avoid board approval is a deliberate breach, and internal audit will find it.

options.text: Analyse it like any other request, on arm's-length terms, send it for board approval and show the related party check in the compliance section.
options.outcome: Correct. Birr 70 million is 1.75% of capital, well within the 15% per related party limit, but above Birr 15 million it needs board approval, and the director must not take part in that decision.

options.text: Refuse: the bank should not lend to companies linked to directors.
options.outcome: The directive does not ban related party lending; it limits and controls it. Refusing a sound request outright is not required and loses business.

tasks.subject: Bole Edible Oil: what if the margin falls to 5%?
body: You present Bole's term loan with a 12-month grace period, which gives a DSCR of 1.25 on a 7% EBIT margin. A committee member asks: 'Bole's margin fell from 9% to 6.5% in three years. What happens at 5%?' You ran the sensitivity last night.

exhibit.title: Bole FY4 with EBIT margin at 5% (Birr thousands)

tasks.ask: What do you tell the committee?

options.text: Assure them the margin will not fall that far: the new line improves efficiency.
options.outcome: You had the answer and did not share it. Committees decide on the downside; an analyst who hides a sensitivity loses the committee's trust for every future proposal.

options.text: Show the 0.96 DSCR and propose protections: a margin covenant, quarterly monitoring, no dividends while DSCR is below 1.25, and an owners' undertaking to inject funds.
options.outcome: Exactly the expected answer: at 5% Bole cannot meet term debt even with grace. The covenants are the early warning, and the owners' undertaking is the backstop. The committee approves with conditions.

options.text: Withdraw the proposal for more work.
options.outcome: The proposal is sound in the base case. The committee needed to hear the downside and how it is controlled, not a withdrawal.

options.text: Re-run the projection at 7.5% so the committee sees a better DSCR.
options.outcome: Answering a downside question with a more optimistic projection is misleading the committee.

tasks.subject: Please release the overdraft today
body: An overdraft for another customer, Dire Sugar Traders, was approved 96 days ago but never drawn. The owner now calls: harvest purchases start Monday and he wants to draw today. The file shows the insurance policy on the pledged warehouse has not been endorsed to the bank.

options.text: Release it today: the approval is on file.
options.outcome: The approval lapsed after 90 days, and a condition precedent, the endorsed insurance, is unmet. Disbursing now breaks two rules at once.

options.text: Explain that the approval has lapsed, send it back for quick re-approval with updated information, and get the endorsed policy before any drawing.
options.outcome: Correct. Re-approval refreshes the information the decision rests on, and the endorsed policy protects the bank's security. Warning the customer today gives him time to arrange both before Monday.

options.text: Release half now and sort out the insurance next week.
options.outcome: A partial release is still a release on a lapsed approval without its conditions precedent.

options.text: Extend the approval by 30 days yourself and release once the insurance is endorsed.
options.outcome: Getting the insurance first is right, but an analyst cannot extend an approval: it goes back to whoever holds the approval authority.

followUps.subject: Adama Flour Mill: the overdraft was approved at Birr 12 million on your fast-track memo
body: Adama Flour Mill's overdraft is fully drawn and has not swung once. Receivables have reached 120 days, one large distributor is disputing invoices, and the RM now asks for an increase to Birr 15 million.

options.text: Increase the limit so the mill can keep operating.
options.outcome: More money into a stuck cycle only grows the exposure that is already at risk. This is how a performing loan becomes a non-performing one.

options.text: Freeze the limit, visit the mill, verify receivables and stock, require additional security and a plan to collect, and watch it for special mention.
options.outcome: The right recovery steps: understand the cause, protect the bank, and classify honestly if it deteriorates. The lesson stands: analyse before you fast-track.

options.text: Call back the full overdraft immediately.
options.outcome: Calling back without a plan pushes a going concern into default and lowers what the bank recovers.

followUps.subject: Truck B cannot be registered as collateral
body: The collateral unit rejects Truck B: it is past the age limit and its insurer will not renew the policy. Metehara Logistics' package was approved on your 130% figure, so actual acceptable coverage is now 105%, and the committee asks why.

options.text: Say the difference is small and leave it.
options.outcome: The committee approved on a wrong figure. Errors in a credit report are corrected in writing, not explained away.

options.text: Correct the coverage in a written memo, confirm 105% is still strongly secured, and ask the committee to note the change.
options.outcome: Owning and correcting the error keeps the file honest. 105% still meets the strongly secured band, so the decision can stand with the corrected figure.

options.text: Ask the customer for another building to restore 130%.
options.outcome: The facility is still strongly secured at 105%. Asking for collateral the policy does not require damages the relationship to cover your own error.

followUps.subject: Five Birr 14 million loans to one related company
body: Internal audit has flagged five Birr 14 million loans to Gara Mulata Trading booked on the same day, all below the board approval threshold. The audit report goes to the board audit committee and must be reported to the NBE.

options.text: Argue that each loan was within your approval authority.
options.outcome: Each loan is part of one exposure to one related party. Splitting is the breach, and defending it makes it worse.

options.text: Acknowledge the breach, consolidate the exposure into one facility and submit it for board approval on arm's-length terms.
options.outcome: Fixing the breach openly is the only way forward. It is also the reason the rule exists: board oversight of lending to insiders.

options.text: Ask the customer to repay two of the loans quickly so the total looks smaller.
options.outcome: Window dressing a breach does not cure it and deepens the problem.

memo.prompt: Write your end-of-week hand-over note to the branch manager.
guide: The two decisions you are most sure of, and why.
The decision you would revisit, and what you would check.
Conditions and covenants that must be followed up next week, with dates.
One risk in the branch portfolio you want the manager to watch.

exam.q: Receivables Birr 8 million, sales Birr 64 million. Receivable days?
Bole's current ratio stayed near 1.55 while its cash conversion cycle grew from 67.7 to 102.5 days. What is the best reading?
options: Bank borrowing inflated both current assets and current liabilities while the cycle slowed
exam.explain: The overdraft grew alongside receivables and stock, hiding the slowdown.

exam.q: Net profit 2,000; depreciation 800; term interest 600; term principal 1,500. DSCR?

A company reports net profit of Birr 2.4 million and depreciation of Birr 1.7 million; receivables rise Birr 3.6 million, inventory Birr 3.0 million and payables Birr 0.5 million. Cash flow from operations?
An auditor's qualification covers Birr 9 million of a borrower's Birr 50 million total assets. How is it classified?
options: Major, minus 5, because it exceeds 15% of total assets
Major only if the loan exceeds Birr 10 million

exam.q: A shareholder loan has no written subordination. In the spread it is:
exam.explain: Only a loan subordinated in writing counts as quasi-equity.

exam.q: Projected receivables Birr 12 million, inventory Birr 15 million, payables Birr 7 million. At a 75% bank share, the overdraft limit is:
A term loan's DSCR is 0.91 in year 1 because a new line is being installed. Which change helps most without adding risk to the bank?
options: A principal grace period during installation, then a test of year 2
exam.explain: Grace matches repayment to when the asset produces cash.

exam.q: A medium-term loan in a typical Ethiopian bank manual is repaid over:
exam.explain: Medium term is 13 to 60 months, excluding grace.

exam.q: Name the weights of the five grading parameters.
options: Financial 35, business 10, management 15, account performance 25, relationship 15
exam.explain: Financial 35, business and industry 10, management 15, account performance 25, relationship 15.

exam.q: A borrower scores 66 and is partially secured. Grade and implication?
options: Grade 3, bankable; cannot be unsecured and an action plan is required
exam.explain: 60 to 69.9 is Grade 3; unsecured lending is for Grades 1 and 2 only.

exam.q: Gedeo Foods PLC is new to the bank and has operated for 8 months. Its starting grade is:
exam.explain: New customers and businesses under one year old start at Grade 3.

exam.q: A 2-year-old vehicle has an insurance value of Birr 2 million and an invoice of Birr 2.2 million. At 90%, its acceptable value is:
exam.explain: 90% of the lower value, Birr 2 million, is Birr 1.8 million.

exam.q: Exposure Birr 35 million; collateral after haircuts Birr 46.9 million. The coverage band is:
Cost of funds 7.5%, operating cost 3%, target margin 3%, term premium 1%, PD 2% and LGD 50%. Rate?
Why are medium and long-term loans priced higher than short-term loans?
options: NBE sets a minimum long-term rate
They carry more uncertainty, tie up funds longer and create a maturity mismatch against mostly short-term deposits
exam.explain: The term premium compensates for time and mismatch risk.

exam.q: A Grade 3 machinery borrower contributes 35% equity on a Birr 10 million excavator. The building required at 45% of the loan is:
exam.explain: Loan = Birr 6.5 million; 45% x 6.5 = Birr 2.925 million.

exam.q: Under SBB/88/2024, exposure to a single related party is limited to:
exam.explain: 15% per related party and 35% in aggregate.

exam.q: Bole's FY4 EBIT margin falls to 5% and DSCR with grace drops to 0.96. Which committee response is strongest?
options: Show the downside, and tie the margin covenant, quarterly monitoring and owner support or a smaller loan to it
exam.explain: Repayment capacity comes first; mitigants must address the named risk.

exam.q: Under SBB/90/2024, the provision rate for a loan classified substandard is:
exam.explain: Pass 1%, special mention 3%, substandard 20%, doubtful 50%, loss 100%.
